name: TESSERA CORPONATION Sentinel DataVault CorpSec BCI
description:
The Sentinel DataVault is TESSERA CORPONATION's flagship corporate-issue BCI, engineered for mid-to-senior employees handling sensitive proprietary data, financial projections, and classified internal communications. The implant features a 512-bit quantum-resistant encryption layer applied to all neural memory consolidation during REM cycles, effectively partitioning work-related cognitive data into a sealed enclave inaccessible to external scanning or neural intrusion attempts. A passive intrusion detection module monitors synaptic I/O traffic in real time, flagging anomalous extraction signatures and triggering a neural firewall lockdown within 0.003 seconds of detection. Compartmentalization protocols allow the device to segment the user's working memory into up to six isolated cognitive partitions, each requiring biometric neural-signature authentication to access — meaning even the user cannot cross-contaminate classified project data without deliberate authorization.

The DataVault is the de facto standard for Tessera's own CorpSec divisions and is widely issued to corporate lawyers, senior analysts, account executives, and compliance officers operating in the mid-Shelf to Ledge tiers of GLMZ's corporate ecosystem. Street workers call it 'the Lockbox' with a mix of contempt and envy — it's a status marker that signals you have secrets worth protecting, and by extension, a salary worth envying. Black-market neural hackers specifically target DataVault users as high-value marks, knowing that a successful extraction yields premium-grade proprietary intelligence. Tessera employees joke grimly that the implant makes them worth more unconscious than alive.
installation_requirements: Certified TESSERA-approved neural clinic; mandatory 72-hour corporate onboarding calibration; employer authorization code required for activation
rejection_risk: Low — military-grade biocompatible housing with adaptive neuro-polymer interface; rejection events are rare but catastrophic when they occur due to deep integration depth
maintenance: Quarterly remote firmware audits via Tessera corporate network; annual in-clinic hardware diagnostic; encryption keys rotated biannually by corporate IT
specifications: {"encryption": "512-bit quantum-resistant AES-QR neural enclave", "partitions": "up to 6 isolated cognitive compartments", "intrusion_detection": "passive synaptic I/O monitoring, 0.003s lockdown response", "data_retention": "secure memory consolidation up to 40TB equivalent indexed recall", "loyalty_verification": "passive stress-pattern baseline monitoring with anomaly flagging", "neural_firewall": "hardware-level killswitch on unauthorized extraction attempt", "power_source": "bioelectric harvesting with 72hr capacitor backup", "form_factor": "dual-lobe cranial implant, 18mm x 9mm per node"}
side_effects: Compartmentalization bleed: users occasionally struggle to emotionally process personal relationships when the implant's partition walls activate during stress, causing affect flattening in off-hours

Intrusion detection hypersensitivity: the passive monitoring system can misread emotional intimacy or alcohol-impaired neural patterns as intrusion attempts, triggering minor headaches and social withdrawal responses
Dream fragmentation: encrypted REM consolidation produces vivid but emotionally incoherent dreams as personal and partitioned memories fail to integrate normally
Corporate dependency syndrome: users who leave Tessera employment often experience significant cognitive disorientation as deactivated partitions create perceived 'holes' in working memory
cultural_context: In GLMZ's corporate culture, a DataVault implant is a double-edged status symbol. It signals that you've ascended high enough to be entrusted with secrets — but also that you're now property of the corp in a very literal neurological sense. Tessera's end-user agreements include clauses allowing the company to remotely audit 'work-partition contents' upon termination of employment, a practice that has spawned an entire underground legal industry of 'neural divorce' specialists who help former employees legally contest post-employment memory audits. On the Ledge, wearing a DataVault scar (a subtle raised ridge behind the left ear) gets you better tables at corp-adjacent restaurants and worse treatment at Shelf-level bars.
known_users: CorpSec operatives requiring compartmentalized mission data
corporate espionage targets who've been 'voluntarily' upgraded
story_hooks: A recently terminated Tessera analyst approaches the crew: her DataVault is still active and Tessera's remote audit team is 48 hours from legally accessing her partitioned memories — which contain evidence of a corporate atrocity she witnessed. She needs someone to physically destroy or extract the implant before the audit window opens.

A DataVault user has been murdered and the implant's neural firewall triggered on extraction, meaning the killer failed to get the data — but the implant is still broadcasting a low-level distress signal that both Tessera's recovery team and a rival corp's extraction unit are homing in on. The crew finds the body first.

A Tessera compliance officer with a DataVault is behaving erratically, convinced that her partition walls are being accessed by someone inside her own company — her loyalty monitoring flags are firing without cause. She's either being gaslit by internal CorpSec, or the implant itself has been compromised in a way Tessera hasn't disclosed.
